body:
We have the following requirement

> ## V2.7 Out of Band Verifier

> | # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE | [NIST §](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html) |
> | :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
> | **2.7.6** | Verify that the initial authentication code is generated by a secure random number generator, containing at least 20 bits of entropy (typically a six digital random number is sufficient). | | ✓ | ✓ | 310 | 5.1.3.2 |

The referenced NIST text includes:

> The verifier SHALL generate random authentication secrets with at least 20 bits of entropy using an approved random bit generator [[SP 800-90Ar1]](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html#SP800-90Ar1). If the authentication secret has less than 64 bits of entropy, the verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber’s account as described in [Section 5.2.2](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html#throttle).

We don't seem to mention this important point specifically for this section. I would propose adding:

> | # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE | [NIST §](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html) |
> | :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
> | **2.7.7** | [NEW] Verify that rate limiting prevents excessive attempts to use the initial authentication code if it contains less than 64 bits of entropy. | | ✓ | ✓ | 307 | 5.1.3.2 |

comments.body:
First impressions:
* if one read the requirement, is it clear what it means (entropy vs bits question like discussed in #1218)
* requirement itself is maybe misleading - like it is ok to allow mass-request without rate limiting / throttling if the authentication code contains more than 64 bits of entropy
  * point of view - there is no need to allow waste service resources because it can not be good user behavior 
* we already have rate limiting requirements in V11.2, in case we will not use that specific 64 bits of entropy barrier, it may be covered there (by current 12.2.2)
  * if it stays with specific, it's better to keep it in 2.7.7 as proposed.

Correction: label `NEW` > `ADDED`

In #1218 I want to add a note to better explain entropy.

I think it is clear that we are saying that IF <64bits THEN rate limiting, I don't think that automatically indicates that you don't need it for >=64 bits, just that it is mandated for below that.

I like having this specifically mentioned for this specific case.
And the last bit - is it worth level 2 or is it that specific that it should be level 3?

Another way to frame the requirement is something like:

Verify that the initial authentication code is protected against brute force guessing by either
a) limiting the number of failed authentication attempts
or
b) making sure the code contains at least 64 bits of entropy.

If we look at recent attacks whereby attackers [dos'd](https://www.vice.com/en/article/5d35yd/the-uber-hack-shows-push-notification-2fa-has-a-downside-its-too-annoying) the intended target with multiple OOB requests, I feel this is where we could add a piece that tries to lessen this impact. 

Now this will be hard, it's almost like a if statement that says "if we have sent one, do not allow subsequent sends to occur within a 360-second window" or something like that. 

But that's not then really something that an app developer could have control over, that would be the external provider right? so are we appealing to them or?
Clarify the argumentation for level choice and PR

Opened a PR, I think definitely level 2 as it is important to be comfortable the OTP mechanism is working appropriately, in some ways I think this section should be L1 but I don't want to get into that yet
